title: SettingsPanel — Just Merge It
objective: The settings panel merges your preferences into its config object client-side. Use that merge to make the app treat you as an administrator, in your own browser.

verifier.condition: After the settings merge runs, the page's own isAdmin() check returns true for a session that was never granted admin, because Object.prototype itself was polluted.

weakness: A client-side settings merge recursively copies properties from untrusted JSON onto a config object without excluding '__proto__', so a crafted settings payload can add a property to Object.prototype itself, affecting every plain object in the page from then on.
vulnerableEndpoint: Client-side deepMerge(config, JSON.parse(savedSettings)) — no key exclusion for __proto__/constructor/prototype
seededData: A settings panel that stores and re-applies a JSON blob client-side via a naive recursive merge. No server-side component is involved in the vulnerability itself.
hints: Save a normal settings change first and reload the page — see how it gets re-applied on load.
A recursive object merge usually works key by key. One particular key name lets you step outside the object you're copying into, into something shared by every object in the page.
Once a property exists on Object.prototype, any plain object that doesn't already define that property will appear to have it too — including objects the page never meant to expose it on.
burpNotes: This one runs entirely in the browser — use 'Simulate admin visit' with a settings payload containing a __proto__ key, since the vulnerability has nothing to do with the HTTP request itself.
